 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,

Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.Ananda.K.S, learned counsel for the appellant who appeared physically before this Court as well as Sri.Jwala Kumar, learned counsel who argued appearing through online and representing respondent No.1-Insurance company.
2. Disputing the validity of the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru in MVC No.2296/2020 dated 02.11.2022, the claimant is before this Court by way of appeal.
Sri. Ananda
. K.S, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appeal is filed raising two pertinent grounds.
Firstly that the negligence attributed on part of the appellant is erroneous and indeed the appellant did not contribute for the accident to occur.
Secondly that the quantum awarded as compensation is minimal and therefore, there is every requirement to enhance the compensation.

4. Arguing on first ground, learned counsel Sri.Ananda.K.S submits that without any iota of proof that is produced by respondent No.1 with regard to the contribution of the appellant for the accident to occur, the Tribunal gave a finding that the appellant is equally liable for the occurrence of the accident and that his contribution is to the extent of 50%.
Learned counsel submits that all the police record is against the driver of the Tempo Traveler which is involved in the accident.

5. On the other hand, the submission made by Sri.Jwala Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.1 is NC: 2024:KHC:32268 that there is head on collusion between two vehicles and therefore, the drivers of both the vehicles are equally at fault and thus the Tribunal fastened the liability as against the appellant also.

sentences.text: The version of the appellant is that on 01.02.2020 at about 4.45 p.m., while he was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04-EQ-4213 on NH-48 Tumkur service road riding the same, the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing registration No.KA-02-AB- 8887 drove his vehicle at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and hit against his vehicle, due to which he fell down and sustained injuries.
It is not in dispute that basing on the contents of Ex.P2-Complaint, a case was registered as in Ex.P1-FIR.

Also it is equally not in dispute that the police investigated in to the case and filed the charge sheet which is evident through the contents of Ex.P7 that due to the negligence of the driver of the Tempo the accident occurred.

As rightly contended by Sri.Ananda.K.S, learned NC: 2024:KHC:32268 counsel for the appellant,
respondent No.1-Insurance company did not led any evidence to show the appellant was at fault.
No documentary or oral evidence is on record to show that due to the negligence on the part of the appellant the accident occurred.

On the other hand, sufficient material both oral and documentary were produced by the appellant to establish that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo vehicle.

Even in the impugned order, there is no discussion with regard to the concept of contributory negligence in detail and as to how and basing on which material the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the appellant contributed for the accident to occur and that his contribution is to an extent of 50%.
Without any substantive proof, it appears the Tribunal only on the premises that there is head on collision between the two vehicles has fastened the liability upon the appellant also.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the finding given to that effect requires interference by this Court which is exercising appellate jurisdiction.

This Court is also of the NC: 2024:KHC:32268 view that the Tribunal erred in attributing the negligence on the part of the appellant as such attribution is not based on any substantive proof or convincing material.

Therefore, this Court holds that the appellant cannot be fastened with any liability.
7.

Coming to the second ground urged i.e., in respect of quantum of compensation that is awarded,
the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.5,50,480/- as compensation divided under following heads:
 Sl. Description Amount  No  1 Loss of future income Rs.3,91,500
2 Loss of income during the  laid up period and one Rs.28,980  attendant charge

3 Conveyance charges Rs.10,000  4 Pain and sufferings Rs.60,000  5 Food nourishment,
 attendant charges and Rs.40,000  loss of amenities

6 Future medical expenses Rs.20,000  Total Rs.5,50,480 Sri Thippeswamy vs The Manager on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138223016/
3  NC: 2024:KHC:32268 8.
As per the material available on record the appellant sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and he was treated as inpatient for a period of 15 days.

The Tribunal considering the whole body disability at 15%, assessing the income as Rs.14,500/- p.m., applying appropriate multiplier 15 has come to a conclusion that loss of future earnings on account of disability is Rs.3,91,500/-.
Also considering the nature of injury sustained, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.28,980/- under the head loss of income during laid up period and charges for one attendant.

The Tribunal besides awarding Rs.60,000/- under the head pain and sufferings, has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards conveyance charges, Rs.40,000/- towards food, nourishment, attendant charges and loss of amenities and Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses.

9. Learned counsel Sri.Jwala Kumar submits that the Tribunal has awarded just compensation under all NC: 2024:KHC:32268 heads and therefore, the award of the Tribunal needs no interference so far as quantum is concerned.

10. Having considered the nature of injury sustained, the treatment taken and the aspect of disability, this Court totally agrees with the findings given by the Tribunal with regard to the compensation awarded under each head.
Sum awarded as compensation is just and reasonable and therefore, the quantum needs no interference.

11. Thus, in the light of the forgoing discussion, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Respondent No.1-Insurance company and respondent No.2-Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the entire amount that is awarded as compensation to the appellant/claimant.
NC: 2024:KHC:32268 (iii) Respondents are directed to deposit the entire compensation within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with accrued interest.
